gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the '45 W' on these banks means once normalised: on the one model with a lab reading (UGREEN Nexode 45W PB603, ChargerLAB) PPS stops at 11 V 3 A (33 W) and 45 W exists only as the fixed 15 V 3 A step, and no page sets the makers' two-device figures side by side (Anker A1638: 15 W cable + 7.5 W port; PB603 label: 5 V 3 A).
standout_why: Talk Android (cited) has no PPS, Wh, input or shared-output figure for any of its six banks and says 45 W is something 'Samsung's fastest phones can use'. The Anker blog (cited) gives only 45 W max, 40 W for iPhone 17 and a 2-hour recharge. Anker's A1638 page (cited) already prints its own 22.5 W combined cap, and itechguides (a result, not cited) repeats Anker's 15 W / 7.5 W split and gives 36 Wh, so the Anker half is not new. Pickstead covers the 30 W A1259 (24 W combined, PPS 3-11 V 2.72 A), not the 45 W models. The new part is the PPS ceiling, which answers the caveat ChatGPT left open for Galaxy Ultra owners, but I could source it only for a sibling UGREEN model, not for the Nexode Pro, Baseus FC11 or INIU. TechRadar's product section was truncated when fetched; Today, NYMag, PopSci, powerbank-online and the Best Buy listing were not opened.
decides: It does not flip the pick. For one phone, every 45 W bank here covers an iPhone. For two devices at once, the Anker retractable drops to 15 W + 7.5 W by Anker's own table, so its price premium buys cable length and not shared power. For a Galaxy owner wanting 45 W, the Anker A1638 is the only bank whose maker page I could open that states 45 W for Samsung. The page must not claim Samsung 45 W for the UGREEN Nexode Pro or the Baseus FC11 until their PPS ranges are read, because the UGREEN sibling ChargerLAB tested tops out at 33 W on PPS. Prices have also moved from ChatGPT's cards: Anker A1638 is $45.99 (card said $59.99) and INIU Pawsible Slim is $26.99 (card said $24.99).
